newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Meralco 1996 net up on robust sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Meralco 1996 net up on robust sales growth.

text.p: The Philippine's biggest electricity distributor, Manila Electric Co (Meralco), posted a 14.8 percent rise in 1996 earnings on better-than-expected sales growth that market analysts said would persist this year.
Meralco on Wednesday reported net income of 5.064 billion pesos ($192 million) in 1996 against 4.411 billion the previous year.
The company said it posted a 12.2 percent increase in kilowatt-hour (kwh) sales to 17.81 billion kwhs last year from 15.88 billion kwhs in 1995.
"The net income last year was really mainly because of kilowatt-hour sales and an increase in customer base," said Francisco Trinidad, research head at DBS Securities Phils Inc.
"They started out with a low base in 1995 due to the typhoons and the favourable weather in 1996 augured well for the company, resulting in lower maintenance costs," Trinidad added.
The company previously said it expected eight percent to 10 percent kwh sales growth in 1996.
Meralco said its customers numbered 2.87 million last year compared with 2.66 million in 1995.
BPI Securities Corp said although Meralco's 1996 net income lined up with its 5.0648 billion forecast, the rise in kwh sales growth was beyond the broker's projected 10.6 percent.
Trinidad said Meralco's expansion of its customer base to depressed areas in Metro Manila and intensified rural electrification activities also helped beef up the company's finances last year.
For 1997, market analysts expect Meralco to duplicate its double-digit growth although at a slower pace from last year.

"We are still very bullish on Meralco this year. We are maintaining a double-digit growth sales at 10.5 percent primarily due to increase in industrial sales," said Cecilio Castro, assistant manager at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
Analysts expect revenues from non-power distribution activities of Meralco to further prop up the company's earnings this year.

Meralco has a 51 percent stake in Rockwell Land Corp. It owns the 15.5 hectare land in Manila's financial district of Makati City that Rockwell Land is converting into a mixed-use commercial and industrial centre.
The power distribution company also has a stake in a 215-megawatt power plant in the northern province of La Union.
ING Baring Securities Phils Inc analyst Giovanni de la Rosa said he expects non-core activities to contribute eight percent to 10 percent of a projected 5.73 billion peso net income this year.
DBS Securities said it expects Meralco's kwh sales to grow by eight percent to 12 percent this year and pegs earnings growth at 10 percent to 11 percent.
BPI Securities, on the other hand, sees Meralco's earnings edging higher by 13 percent this year to 5.7 billion pesos.
